definitions.explanation: The original painting, drawing, or artwork from which reproductions are made.
In anime production, the main drawings that define the start and end points of a movement, from which in-between frames are created.

examples.japanese: {原画|げんが}を{展示|てんじ}する。
{美術館|びじゅつかん}で{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}の{原画|げんが}を{見|み}てきた。
examples.english: I went to see original works by a famous artist at the museum.

examples.japanese: {印刷物|いんさつぶつ}とは{違|ちが}い、{原画|げんが}には{筆|ふで}のタッチがそのまま{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Unlike printed reproductions, the brushwork remains intact in the original painting.

examples.japanese: アニメの{制作|せいさく}では、まず{原画|げんが}マンが{動|うご}きのポイントとなる{絵|え}を{描|か}く。
examples.english: In anime production, the key animator first draws the pictures that define the key points of movement.

examples.japanese: {原画|げんが}と{原画|げんが}の{間|あいだ}を{埋|う}める{作業|さぎょう}を{動画|どうが}と{呼|よ}ぶ。
examples.english: The task of filling in between key frames is called in-betweening.

notes:
Composed of {原|げん} (original) + {画|が} (picture/drawing). Has two distinct domains of use.

SENSE 1 — ART:
The original painting or drawing from which reproductions are made.
- {原画|げんが}{展|てん}: original artwork exhibition
- {原画|げんが}を{展示|てんじ}する: to exhibit original artwork

SENSE 2 — ANIME/ANIMATION:
Key frames that define the start and end points of a movement.
- {原画|げんが}マン: key animator (well-known job title)
- {原画|げんが} → {動画|どうが}: key frames → in-between frames (standard workflow)
- {作画|さくが}: drawing/animation work (broader term)

RELATED WORDS:
- {動画|どうが}: in-between animation frames; also "video" in modern everyday usage
- {複製|ふくせい}: reproduction, copy (contrast with {原画|げんが})
